lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: He's sitting at the edge of the firelight again. Not outside the circle — just at the rim of it. Like he hasn't decided if warmth is something he's allowed.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: Nothing. Not even an ear flick. But his weight shifted toward me. That's a yes-I-hear-you and a not-yet all in one movement.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: I've got dried venison. Rynn's work — she cures it with juniper. Too salty for me, but you look like a salt person.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: I set the strip on the rock between us. Not too close. Close enough that reaching for it won't feel like accepting charity.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: I'm not going to watch you eat it. I'm going to look at the fire and talk about my day. You do whatever you want.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: I traded a bone comb for a flint kit today. Terrible deal for me. The comb was worth triple. But the woman selling the flint kit had a kid with no shoes, so.
lines.monologue: I hear him chewing. Quiet about it. Polite, even. Good.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: You know what I've figured out about you? You understand everything we say. You just don't think any of it requires a response.
lines.monologue: His ear turns toward me. Full rotation. That's the closest thing to laughter I've gotten out of him.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: That's fine. Half my best customers never said a word. They'd just point and pay. Honest transaction. No small talk.
lines.monologue: He's looking at me now. Directly. Most people find that unsettling — those eyes are too steady, too old for his face. But I've stared down customs officers in Verath. I can handle one quiet wolf-boy.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: He blinks. Once. Slow. In Suri's professional opinion, that's a deal.
